statusText:
The CME weekend halt still governs the published state. NQ has not quoted since Friday's close and does not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC tonight, so Tail holds at 13% (low), the action is EA_ON and the status is green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. No pathological one-way price path can form while no venue is quoting.

This hour produced no new escalation, and the assessment says so rather than manufacturing a move. The Times of Israel liveblog has added nothing since the 08:29 IDT entry naming Ali Muhammad Fakhr al-Din as the second senior Hezbollah commander killed in Saturday's Deir al-Zahrani strike, which was already scored two hours ago. The Russia-Ukraine round scored last hour - roughly 600 Ukrainian drones toward the Moscow region, Russia's ballistic answer on Kyiv and Kryvyi Rih - is unchanged on re-check, with today's incremental reporting confined to casualty accounting and a Dnipropetrovsk territorial claim rather than any new target class. No refinery, pipeline or export terminal has been struck, so the energy transmission channel that would carry this to the Nasdaq is still shut.

Stress therefore moves only one point, 78% to 79%, and it is bought by the single thing that genuinely changed: an hour less until a thin Globex restart auction has to absorb an entire weekend of two live theatres at once. It is not bought by new headlines, because there were none. Stress stays inside the high band.

Confidence rises to 73% (solid). Every cross-asset mark was re-verified from primary sources this hour and came back unchanged - NQ September 30,141.75, VIX 14.25, 2Y 4.15%, 10Y 4.63%, WTI $82.40, Brent $88.52 - and the evidence set gained one datum it did not have before: the Nasdaq-100 cash index close of 30,046.14, verified independently at Yahoo Finance, which puts the cash index about 2.3% below its 52-week high and corroborates the futures picture rather than merely repeating it.
recommendation:
Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 13% maps to EA_ON for both instruments. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to defend against while the venue is shut. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The actionable item this hour is scheduling, not sizing.

The roughly 22:00 UTC CME Globex restart is the only checkpoint inside this forecast window, and the danger window is anchored to it at 22:00-02:00 UTC (00:00-04:00 Berlin) rather than to the generation time. Forecast Tail drifts 13% to 19% through the remaining halt, steps to 21% at 21:00 UTC and 26% across the first two hours of live quoting - turning the forecast status yellow (WATCH) at 21:00 UTC and orange (BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES) at 22:00 and 23:00 UTC - then eases back through the watch band and returns to green at 05:00 UTC Monday. That orange is conditional forecast risk, not observed structure. It says a thin opening auction has to price an undelivered Hezbollah retaliation, a record-scale Russia-Ukraine exchange and a still-closed Strait of Hormuz against a VIX that last printed at 14.25 and has discounted none of it.

No US macro release lands inside the next 24 hours. Monday's Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC is the first, and Wednesday's July FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC are the week's first genuinely high-impact print. This is general market-state analysis for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice, and nothing here is a trade instruction.
headline: Quiet hour inside the CME weekend halt: no new escalation in either live theatre, so Tail holds at 13% and status stays green while Stress buys just one point to 79% on time-to-reopen compression - Nasdaq-100 cash close 30,046.14 added as fresh corroboration, Confidence 73%
body:
Price path: none exists. The current hour and the first thirteen forecast slots sit inside the CME weekend halt, so there is no session direction, no gap, no retracement structure, no failed pullback and no proximity to session extremes to score. Every price input is a Friday carry-forward. That is simultaneously the correct reason for Tail to be low and the correct reason for Confidence to sit in the solid band rather than the high band.

Friday's marks, re-verified from primary sources this hour and unchanged. NQ September futures 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15%, day range 30,028.50-30,283.00 against a 30,188.50 previous close, the quote page explicitly marking the contract closed as of 14 August; the 52-week range is 22,961.50-30,975.50, putting NQ roughly 2.7% below its 52-week high. VIX 14.25, -0.38 or -2.60%, range 14.18-14.72, 52-week range 13.38-35.30, also marked closed at 14 August. WTI $82.40 (+1.42% on the day, about +5% on the week, +32.95% on the year) and Brent $88.52 (+1.67%, +34.43% on the year). US 2-year 4.15% and 10-year 4.63% from the Federal Reserve's H.15 release at the 13 August observation, both lower on the week - the 2-year down 4bp and the 10-year down 2bp from 7 August.

One datum is new to the evidence set this hour, and it is a corroboration rather than a repetition. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Friday at 30,046.14, -38.36 or -0.13%, day range 29,934.66-30,179.82, 52-week range 22,841.42-30,762.20, timestamped 14 August 17:15 EDT at Yahoo Finance. Cash and futures therefore agree on both the magnitude and the direction of Friday's drift, and the cash index sits about 2.3% below its own 52-week high. Until now the "near but not at extremes" reading rested on the futures quote alone; it now rests on two independent venues. That is why Confidence goes to 73% rather than decaying with the age of the marks.

The cross-asset set remains internally conflicting, and conflict is a Stress input rather than a Tail input. Index futures and cash are near - not at - 52-week highs, implied volatility is priced for calm on a 14 handle, duration is bid rather than offered, and only crude is expressing a geopolitical premium. Nothing in it is aligned into a one-way equity structure, and none of it can be aligned into one while the venue is shut. dominantMode stays mixed.

What changed in the news this hour: nothing material, and that is the finding rather than an absence of effort. The Times of Israel liveblog was re-read and its newest market-relevant entries are still the 08:29 IDT IDF confirmation naming Ali Muhammad Fakhr al-Din as the second senior Hezbollah commander killed at Deir al-Zahrani after a Hezbollah drone attack wounded three soldiers, Defence Minister Katz's 07:23 IDT vow to settle scores on all fronts, and the 02:07 IDT strikes in south Lebanon preceded by resident warnings. All three were scored in earlier hours and are not re-counted. The Russia-Ukraine theatre added to the assessment last hour was re-checked and the incremental reporting is casualty accounting and a Ukrainian claim of 745 square kilometres recaptured in Dnipropetrovsk this year, plus the fires in two Kyiv districts and the one death and six injuries at Kryvyi Rih already scored. Crucially, the target class has not changed: warehouses, logistics centres and residential districts, not a refinery, pipeline or export terminal. The oil channel that would make this a Nasdaq problem remains closed.

The Hormuz configuration was checked against a second source this hour and is unchanged but usefully sharpened. The strait has been largely blocked by Iran since 28 February, the reinstated US naval blockade has redirected 49 vessels since mid-July, and transit volumes are running at a handful of ships a day. The Iran-Oman track that earlier hours read as a constructive off-ramp is narrower than the "very close" language suggests: the negotiation covers vessel movement and navigation routes - entry via Iranian-controlled routes, exit via Omani-controlled routes, no tolls - and a senior Iranian lawmaker has stated the talks are in no way about reopening the strait, with Tehran conditioning any reopening on the US lifting the blockade. That is a modest downgrade of the off-ramp, not an escalation, and it does not by itself move Stress; it is recorded because the previous framing overstated how much relief was actually on the table.

Why Stress moves one point and not seven. Last hour's seven-point step was the correction of a real coverage gap - a second live theatre that had not been scored at all. That correction is now made, and repeating it would be double-counting. The rule adopted at 05:00 UTC still governs: a Stress point has to be bought by new evidence. The one point bought this hour is time-to-reopen compression, which is genuine, because the quantity of unpriced weekend risk waiting for a single thin auction increases mechanically as that auction gets closer, and the last volatility mark on the tape is a 14 handle from before any of it happened. That is worth one point. It is not worth more, because no new headline arrived.

Calendar, re-verified against Trading Economics this hour. The next seven days contain no CPI, PPI, PCE, NFP or FOMC rate decision. Empire State and NAHB on Monday, then a dense Tuesday - Housing Starts, Building Permits, Export and Import Prices and the NY Fed Services survey at 12:30 UTC, Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization at 13:15 UTC, Pending Home Sales at 14:00 UTC - the July FOMC minutes Wednesday at 18:00 UTC alongside a 20-year auction at 17:00 UTC, jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey Thursday at 12:30 UTC, and the S&P Global flash PMIs Friday at 13:45 UTC. The API crude stock change at Tuesday 20:30 UTC appeared on this hour's calendar read and has been added on that verified basis. Retail earnings dominate the corporate week - Home Depot Tuesday, Target, Lowe's and TJX Wednesday, Walmart Thursday - so no megacap or semiconductor print capable of creating index-level one-way structure falls inside the window. The two largest scheduled catalysts sit just outside the seven days and are correctly absent from the events array: Nvidia's Q2 FY2027 report on 26 August and the Jackson Hole symposium on 27-29 August.

Why Tail stays at 13%: the strategy-killing condition is persistent directional efficiency with failed retracements and repeated extension. With no venue quoting there is no efficiency, no retracement and no extension to observe, and the last observed session was a quiet -0.15% futures drift inside a 254-point range, corroborated by a -0.13% cash close. Nothing in a closed market can promote a headline into a price path, however large the headline.

Research note on egress: CNBC returned HTTP 403 to this environment on the week-ahead article and was substituted with Yahoo Finance for the cash index and Trading Economics for the calendar. All other primary sources fetched cleanly.

lookbackSummary:
The trailing 24 hours run from 09:00 UTC Saturday to 08:00 UTC Sunday and are entirely inside the CME weekend halt. Claude published in every one of those hours, and the action was EA_ON, the status green and dominantMode mixed for all 24. Tail never left the low band, drifting 10% to 13%. Stress carried the movement: 51, 52, 53, 53, 54, 55, 56, 58, 57, 60, 62, 65, 67, 67, 68, 70, 71, 73, 74, 75, then 70, 71, 71 and 78.

Two features of that track matter for reading the current hour. The first twenty slots are a near-monotonic 24-point climb across a market that never quoted once, in which each hour re-priced the same standing Middle East headlines slightly higher rather than re-testing them; the 05:00 slot is the deliberate correction that stopped it, taken after re-verifying Friday's cross-asset marks against primary sources, and the flat 70-71-71 stretch reflects the rule adopted there, that a Stress point must be bought by new evidence. Confidence rebuilt in parallel from 59% to 70% as those marks were checked hour by hour.

The 08:00 slot's seven-point step to 78% is a different kind of move and is not drift: it added the Russia-Ukraine theatre, which the preceding 23 slots had omitted entirely even while the largest strike on the Moscow region of the war was already being reported. Past opinions are not rewritten - each slot records what was published at the time - but that step is now complete, which is precisely why the current hour does not repeat it.
outlookSummary:
The next 24 hours end at 08:00 UTC Monday, so the roughly 22:00 UTC CME restart and the first ten hours after it are inside the window. Tail stays in the low band for 12 of 24 slots, drifting 13% to 19% as the restart approaches, then stepping to 21% at 21:00 UTC and 26% across the first two hours of live quoting before easing through 24%, 23%, 22%, 21% and 20% and returning to 19% and green at 05:00 UTC Monday. The forecast status is yellow (WATCH) at 21:00 UTC, orange (BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES) at 22:00 and 23:00 UTC, then yellow through 04:00 UTC Monday.

Stress rises from 79% to an 83% plateau across 18:00-21:00 UTC into the reopen, holding at the top of the high band rather than crossing into extreme, then easing to 74% by 08:00 UTC Monday as live price discovery starts converting headline risk into an actual mark. The plateau rather than a spike is deliberate: unpriced weekend risk does compound while the venue is shut, but the two live theatres have both stopped short of the energy-infrastructure transmission channel, and without that channel opening there is no basis for an extreme reading. Confidence decays from 73% to 65% as Friday's marks age, then recovers to 74% after the restart, a larger recovery than the decay because a live price path is the single missing input. The seven slots spanning 21:00 UTC to 03:00 UTC switch to event/whipsaw for a thin opening auction that has to absorb a full weekend at once.

No US macro release falls inside the window; Monday's Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC is the first, and Wednesday's July FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC are the week's first high-impact catalyst. The forecast Tail path is conditional risk, not an assertion that any future price structure has already been observed.

forecastDetail.comment: Current hour. CME Globex has been shut since Friday's close, so there is no price path, no retracement structure and no extension to score; Tail holds at 13% on a Friday carry-forward and the action stays EA_ON. Stress ticks 78% to 79% purely as time-to-reopen compresses against a two-theatre weekend that no venue has priced.

Still inside the halt with European desks closed. Nothing can promote a headline into a price path; Tail unchanged. The only live variable is whether a new Middle East or Russia-Ukraine round lands before the restart auction.
Weekend drift continues. Friday's marks are now roughly 44 hours old, so Confidence begins its decay while Tail stays anchored to an unchanged low reading.
Stress reaches 80% and the top of the high band as the unpriced weekend accumulates against a VIX that last printed 14.25. Tail is unaffected: a closed venue cannot produce directional efficiency.
Asian desks approach their Monday preparation window but no quoting venue is open for NQ. Assessment remains a carry-forward with decaying evidence freshness.
Final slot before the second half of the halt. Tail 15% is still comfortably low; the whole risk of this forecast sits in the 22:00 UTC restart, not in any hour before it.
